issue.body:
## Environment

Ubuntu clang version 18.1.3 (1ubuntu1)
Target: x86_64-pc-linux-gnu
Thread model: posix
InstalledDir: /usr/bin

operating system: ubuntu 24.04
clang is installed using apt.


## Minimal Reproduction Sample

https://godbolt.org/z/9YrKzxKrK
```c
// armtest.c
int main(void) {
  	register float a0 asm("v0");

  	for (int i = 0; i < 2; ++i) {
  		__asm__ volatile("nop" : [a0] "+w"(a0)::);
  	}

  	return 0;
}
```

compiling command:
```bash
clang --target=aarch64-linux-gnu armtest.c -O1
```

for comparison, gcc works well:
```bash
aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc armtest.c -O1
```

## Additional Notes

1. set optimization level to `-O0` will not cause crash
2. another way to avoid crash is to include `arm_neon.h` and change the type of `a0` from `float` to `float32x4_t`
3. I think the error message may be misleading since the cursor in the message is pointed to the `nop` instruction. It crashes no matter what the instructions are.

comments.author: davemgreen
comments.body:
I would expect the float variable to use register "s0". "h0"/"s0"/"d0" are the proper names of f16/f32/f64 variables, if you wanted something that was more valid.

If GCC supports "v0" generrically too (and that isn't a bug), then it sounds OK to treat it the same in LLVM.

comments.author: AlexeyMerzlyakov
comments.body:
@davemgreen from some experiments I've made, it looks like GCC works if specify "h0/s0/d0" as well as using "v0" in inline assembler. Moreover, in this example GCC supposes that `asm("nop" : [a0] "+w"(a0)::)` will re-write `v0` (as we intentionally set it) but in reality it does not happen with "nop". So, it will cause the value of `v0` to be undefined after nop. But this is something like related more how GCC optimizes (I also observed some more strange cases when playing with more inline asms on GCC). In any way, GCC works with `v`-registers in inline asm, and its behavior does not change if replace them to `d/s/h` intentionally set registers.

I am more puzzled about `h0` in LLVM. If change `v0` -> to `h0` in the example from above (`s0` and `d0` works), LLVM will get back with `unknown register name` message, while GCC works with it. Now, checking - whether it is the lack of "H" registers support, or intentionally made restriction. If this is the lack of support, it might be better to restrict patch only to 32- and 64-bit floating point values treating `v` as scalars.

comments.author: AlexeyMerzlyakov
comments.body:
Some update on `h0` case: it seem that B/H/Q registers are missing in the clang front-end, while in the `AArch64RegisterInfo.td` right correct descriptions are already present. So, it could be added to `clang/lib/Basic/Targets/AArch64.cpp`, which I think could be done later in a separate 2nd PR (to be consecutive and not mix two different tasks, test-cases, etc...). 

I'll update 1st PR (ICE bugfix), according to the last experiments findings.

issue.title: clang crashes when compiling aarch64 inline assembly with optimization enabled
